chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Three people, their supplication is returned upon them: a man whom Allah granted wealth, so he spent it in other than its proper way, then he says, "O Lord, grant me sustenance," so it is said to him, "Did I not grant you?"'
And a man who supplicates against his wife while he is unjust to her, so it is said to him, "Did I not make her matter in your hand?"'
And a man who sits in his house and says, "O Lord, grant me sustenance," so it is said to him, "Did I not make for you the way to seek sustenance?"'

key_terms.غَيْرِ وَجْهِهِ: in other than its proper way/purpose

ai.seo_question: Why is a person's supplication rejected if they are unjust or lazy?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the conditions for the acceptance of du'a by identifying three specific spiritual and practical failures: mismanagement of blessings, domestic injustice, and passive reliance without effort. In Shia scholarship, these examples illustrate that supplication is not a substitute for righteous action or justice, but rather a complement to them, emphasizing the balance between divine decree and human agency.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh who said,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Three (people), their supplication would not be returned upon them – a man whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> had Graced wealth but he spent it in other than His<sup>azwj</sup> ways, then says, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Grace me sustenance’, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would Say to him: “Did I<sup>azwj</sup> not Grace you (before)?”.

And a man who supplicates against his unjust wife, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Say to him: “Did I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> not Make her matter to be in your hands?”;

and a man who sits in his house and says, ‘O Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Grace me sustenance’, so He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would be Saying to him: “Did I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> not Make the way for you to seek the sustenance?”’.
en.sarwar: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from al-Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘The prayer of three kinds of people is not accepted: a man to whom Allah has granted wealth but spends it improperly and then says, “O Lord, grant me wealth,” to him it is said, ‘Did I not give you wealth?’
A man who prays against his unjust wife, and it is said to him, ‘Have I not left her affairs to you (dissolving of marriage lawful)?’
A man who sits idle and prayers, ‘O Lord, grant me sustenance,’ and to him it is said, ‘Have I not made ways how to make a living?”’
